newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London up, HSBC firm.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London up, HSBC firm.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks trading in London pushed higher on Thursday, building on the Hang Seng's ascent to another record close, dealers said.
Volume was quiet, they said, with attention centred on HSBC Holdings which rose on the back of a firmer FTSE.
By 1509 GMT the Hang Seng London Reference index had climbed 37.44 points to 13,868.12. HSBC was trading at HK$182.25, up HK$1-1/4 from its record Hong Kong close.
"We opened on a steady note, with HSBC leading the way on a firm FTSE," a dealer said. "There was no real interest in other stocks but they were dragged up in sympathy."
A firmer Dow and long bond were helping boost prices, he said.
In Hong Kong the Hang Seng closed at 13,830.68 after earlier touching a record peak of 14,004.93. Turnover was the third highest ever recorded.
